correctness.rationale: Conditioning on exactly k occupied cells produces a uniform surjection onto the occupied labels. Pearson's statistic is an affine function of the number U of colliding unordered observation pairs. A single collision constraint merges two observations and gives probability S(N-1,k)/S(N,k); any two distinct collision constraints create exactly two identifications, whether the pairs overlap or not, and give joint probability S(N-2,k)/S(N,k). These facts yield the displayed first two moments. Exact rational enumeration over every count vector for 2<=m<=6 and 2<=N<=7 reproduces the formulas in every feasible conditioning stratum.

value.rationale: The number of empty cells is a standard diagnostic of sparse multinomial data, and prior work explicitly modifies Pearson's statistic according to this count. The result gives the exact finite-sample baseline mean and variance of Pearson's statistic within every observed sparsity stratum, rather than only an unconditional law or an asymptotic warning. The formulas are compact, interpretable through pair collisions, and can serve as a finite calibration benchmark for sparse equiprobable goodness-of-fit problems.
